title: Johann Heinrich Kauderbach (The Hague) to Dresden, 1754-56, intercepted despatches with passages in figures (KHA Prins Willem V inv. 201, DECODE R1043-R2082)

steps.what: DECODE records fetched with the session cookie: 32 page images, 3 transcriptions (R1043, R1044, R2078).
Web search for a printed decipherment or edition of Kauderbach's despatches.
Digit counts, successor table, 2- and 3-figure phase IC on the DECODE transcriptions: no fixed period; long exact repeats show a fixed code.
Seven records transcribed from the images by sub-agents (one died on an oversized-image error and was re-run); R1954 in a letter-like hand only partly reliable.
Mixed 1/2/3-figure group rules by first digit scored by entropy; EM segmentation of 1-4-figure tokens.
Removing 5 and 8 as single-figure nulls restores a clean 2-figure phase (IC 0.027 vs 0.021; 4-figure 0.155/0.161 vs 0.103); Viterbi realignment gives a table of about 60 two-figure codes.

Homophonic letter solver (quadgram coordinate ascent, validated 98% on synthetic French through the same pipeline) in French, German, Dutch, Italian, word-reversed French, with nulls, syllable values or merged look-alike figures.
Pattern cribs for long repeats (guerre, Angleterre) seeded into the solver.

DECODE key listing searched; Kauderbach's 1761 key (R936) fetched: one code per letter or syllable, capitals for names, a declared null. Numbers do not fit; vocabulary adopted (m restored from the image).
Simulated annealing over one-to-one assignments of the codes onto the 1761 vocabulary, char-4-gram score; seeds 22 and 24 converged to the same key (-3.85/letter).
Key refined by reading and an extended vocabulary (in, ou, qu, st, par, pas, qui, pour, fai, ke, z; 01/12 swapped); ten letters read by two sub-agents, one per five letters.
Content checked against history: Holderness's warning and the 30,000-man augmentation (Jul 1755), Kniphausen at Compiegne, the Treaty of Versailles of 1 May 1756 with its neutrality clause.

outcome.method_basis: Nulls and the two-figure code table were found by statistics, and the code values were recovered by simulated annealing onto the plaintext vocabulary (letters and syllables) of Kauderbach's 1761 key (DECODE R936), whose numbers do not fit this 1754-58 table.
outcome.notes: fraction_read = share of the 8,512 groups carrying a key value (only 10, 20, 40, 90 guessed, 12 occurrences). Readers estimate 65-97% of the text read in sense per letter; R1954 weakest; the clear sigla are read from context only.

prior.where: DECODE notes that the Hague cabinet never solved them; no printed decipherment found.

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code with Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.
